claims.text: typical symptoms: itching, soreness, external dysuria (burning when urine touches irritated skin), pain with sex, abnormal discharge; none specific
claims.quote: Typical symptoms of VVC include pruritus, vaginal soreness, dyspareunia, external dysuria, and abnormal vaginal discharge. None of these symptoms is specific for VVC.

claims.text: thick, curd-like discharge; redness, swelling, fissures, excoriations
claims.quote: Signs include vulvar edema, fissures, excoriations, and thick curdy vaginal discharge.

claims.text: an estimated 75 percent of women have at least one episode; 40 to 45 percent have two or more
claims.quote: An estimated 75% of women will have at least one episode of VVC, and 40%–45% will have two or more episodes.

claims.text: VVC classified as uncomplicated or complicated based on presentation, organism, host factors and response to therapy
claims.quote: On the basis of clinical presentation, microbiology, host factors, and response to therapy, VVC can be classified as either uncomplicated or complicated

claims.text: uncomplicated: sporadic or infrequent, mild to moderate, likely C. albicans, not immunocompromised
claims.quote: Uncomplicated: "Sporadic or infrequent VVC" AND "Mild-to-moderate VVC" AND "Likely to be Candida albicans" AND "Nonimmunocompromised women"

claims.text: complicated: recurrent, severe, non-albicans, or diabetes, immunocompromising condition such as HIV, immunosuppressive therapy such as corticosteroids
claims.quote: Complicated: "Recurrent VVC" OR "Severe VVC" OR "Non-albicans candidiasis" OR "Women with diabetes, immunocompromising conditions (e.g., HIV infection), underlying immunodeficiency," OR "immunosuppressive therapy (e.g., corticosteroids)"

claims.text: over-the-counter regimens are for uncomplicated VVC; short courses effective
claims.quote: Short-course topical formulations (i.e., single dose and regimens of 1–3 days) effectively treat uncomplicated VVC.

claims.text: recurrent VVC defined as three or more episodes in under a year; affects under 5 percent of women
claims.quote: Recurrent VVC, usually defined as three or more episodes of symptomatic VVC in <1 year, affects <5% of women

claims.text: frequent antibiotic use and diabetes are recognized causes of (secondary) recurrent infection; look for underlying causes
claims.quote: Recurrent VVC can be either idiopathic or secondary (related to frequent antibiotic use, diabetes, or other underlying host factors).

claims.text: severe VVC: extensive erythema, edema, excoriation, fissures
claims.quote: Severe VVC (i.e., extensive vulvar erythema, edema, excoriation, and fissure formation) is associated with lower clinical response rates

claims.text: severe VVC: 7 to 14 days topical azole or two fluconazole 150 mg doses 72 hours apart; complicated cases need longer courses (often 7 to 14 days)
claims.quote: Either 7–14 days of topical azole or 150 mg of fluconazole in two sequential oral doses (second dose 72 hours after initial dose) is recommended.

claims.text: poorly controlled diabetes or immunosuppression: may not respond to short courses; correct modifiable conditions; 7 to 14 day treatment
claims.quote: might not respond as well to short-term therapies. Efforts to correct modifiable conditions should be made, and more prolonged (i.e., 7–14 days) conventional treatment is necessary.

claims.text: symptomatic VVC more frequent with HIV, tracking immunodeficiency
claims.quote: Symptomatic VVC is also more frequent among women with HIV infection and similarly correlates with severity of immunodeficiency

claims.text: VVC associated with normal vaginal pH below 4.5 (text, table, pH figure)
claims.quote: Candida vaginitis is associated with normal vaginal pH (<4.5).

claims.text: pH above 4.5 common with BV or trichomoniasis; trichomoniasis can have normal pH; pH figure
claims.quote: an elevated pH (i.e., >4.5) is common with BV or trichomoniasis (although trichomoniasis can also be present with a normal vaginal pH).

claims.text: pH testing not highly specific, so microscopy follows
claims.quote: Because pH testing is not highly specific, vaginal discharge should be further examined microscopically

claims.text: 10% KOH clears cellular material so yeast is easier to see
claims.quote: Use of 10% KOH in wet preparations improves the visualization of yeast and mycelia by disrupting cellular material that might obscure the yeast or pseudohyphae.

claims.text: budding yeast, hyphae or pseudohyphae on wet prep, or positive culture, supports diagnosis in symptomatic women
claims.quote: a wet preparation (saline, 10% KOH) of vaginal discharge demonstrates budding yeasts, hyphae, or pseudohyphae, or a culture or other test yields a positive result for a yeast species.

claims.text: microscopy sensitivity about 50 percent vs culture; negative result does not rule out yeast
claims.quote: absence of trichomonads in saline or fungal elements in KOH samples does not rule out these infections because the sensitivity of microscopy is approximately 50% compared with NAAT (trichomoniasis) or culture (yeast)

claims.text: yeast culture is the reference standard
claims.quote: Yeast culture, which can identify a broad group of pathogenic yeasts, remains the reference standard for diagnosis.

claims.text: consider culture when wet mount negative but symptoms present
claims.quote: For those with negative wet mounts but existing signs or symptoms, vaginal cultures for Candida should be considered.

claims.text: usually caused by Candida albicans (citable summary)
claims.quote: VVC usually is caused by Candida albicans but can occasionally be caused by other Candida species or yeasts.

claims.text: culture or PCR in complicated VVC; susceptibility testing for patients who remain symptomatic
claims.quote: Vaginal culture or PCR should be obtained from women with complicated VVC to confirm clinical diagnosis

claims.text: susceptibility testing for patients who remain symptomatic
claims.quote: culture and susceptibility testing should be considered for patients who remain symptomatic.

claims.text: uncomplicated: single 150 mg oral fluconazole
claims.quote: Fluconazole 150 mg orally in a single dose

claims.text: topical regimens such as miconazole, clotrimazole, terconazole
claims.quote: Clotrimazole 1% cream 5 g intravaginally daily for 7–14 days ... Miconazole 2% cream 5 g intravaginally daily for 7 days ... Terconazole 0.4% cream 5 g intravaginally daily for 7 days

claims.text: azoles relieve symptoms and clear cultures in 80 to 90 percent who complete therapy
claims.quote: Treatment with azoles results in relief of symptoms and negative cultures in 80%–90% of patients who complete therapy.

claims.text: non-albicans: 7 to 14 days non-fluconazole azole; boric acid 600 mg vaginally once daily for 3 weeks if recurrence
claims.quote: a longer duration of therapy (7–14 days) with a nonfluconazole azole regimen (oral or topical) is recommended. If recurrence occurs, 600 mg of boric acid in a gelatin capsule administered vaginally once daily for 3 weeks is indicated.

claims.text: VVC occurs frequently during pregnancy
claims.quote: VVC occurs frequently during pregnancy.

claims.text: pregnancy: only topical azoles for 7 days
claims.quote: Only topical azole therapies, applied for 7 days, are recommended for use among pregnant women.

claims.text: pregnancy: single 150 mg fluconazole might be associated with miscarriage and birth defects; should not be used
claims.quote: Epidemiologic studies indicate a single 150-mg dose of fluconazole might be associated with spontaneous abortion () and congenital anomalies; therefore, it should not be used ().

claims.text: a past clinician diagnosis does not make self-diagnosis reliable
claims.quote: Even women who have previously received a diagnosis of VVC by a clinician are not necessarily more likely to be able to diagnose themselves

claims.text: evaluate and test if symptoms persist after OTC product or return within two months
claims.quote: any woman whose symptoms persist after using an over-the-counter preparation or who has a recurrence of symptoms <2 months after treatment for VVC should be evaluated clinically and tested.

claims.text: history alone not enough; careful history, examination and laboratory testing to find the cause of vaginal symptoms
claims.quote: Obtaining a medical history alone has been reported to be insufficient for accurate diagnosis of vaginitis and can lead to inappropriate administration of medication

claims.text: careful history, examination and laboratory testing warranted
claims.quote: a careful history, examination, and laboratory testing to determine the etiology of any vaginal symptoms are warranted.

claims.text: uncomplicated VVC not usually acquired through sex; data do not support treating partners
claims.quote: Uncomplicated VVC is not usually acquired through sexual intercourse, and data do not support treatment of sex partners.

claims.text: balanitis on the glans in a minority of male partners
claims.quote: A minority of male sex partners have balanitis, characterized by erythematous areas on the glans of the penis in conjunction with pruritus or irritation.

claims.text: fishy (amine) odor suggests BV or trichomoniasis
claims.quote: samples that emit an amine odor immediately upon application of KOH suggest BV or trichomoniasis

claims.text: trichomoniasis discharge diffuse, foul-smelling or yellow-green, with or without vulvar irritation
claims.quote: women with trichomoniasis sometimes have vaginal discharge, which can be diffuse, malodorous, or yellow-green with or without vulvar irritation

claims.text: motile trichomonads and clue cells on saline microscopy
claims.quote: The saline-solution specimen might display motile trichomonads or clue cells (i.e., epithelial cells with borders obscured by small anaerobic bacteria), which are characteristic of BV.

claims.text: BV: thin, milky discharge, fishy odor, pH above 4.5
claims.quote: Homogeneous, thin discharge (milklike consistency) that smoothly coats the vaginal walls

claims.text: BV fishy odor criterion
claims.quote: A fishy odor of vaginal discharge before or after addition of 10% KOH (i.e., the whiff test)

claims.text: BV treated with metronidazole or clindamycin
claims.quote: Metronidazole 500 mg orally 2 times/day for 7 days ... Clindamycin cream 2% one full applicator (5 g) intravaginally at bedtime for 7 days

claims.text: trichomoniasis treated with metronidazole; tinidazole alternative
claims.quote: Metronidazole 500 mg 2 times/day for 7 days ... Tinidazole 2 g orally in a single dose

claims.text: trichomoniasis: treatment of all sex partners
claims.quote: Concurrent treatment of all sex partners is vital for preventing reinfections.

claims.text: inflammation without pathogens points to mechanical, chemical, allergic or other noninfectious cause
claims.quote: Presence of objective signs of vulvovaginal inflammation in the absence of vaginal pathogens after laboratory testing indicates the possibility of mechanical, chemical, allergic, or other noninfectious causes of vulvovaginal signs or symptoms.

claims.text: pelvic or lower abdominal pain can signal PID
claims.quote: if they are experiencing pelvic or lower abdominal pain, if no cause for the illness other than PID can be identified

claims.text: clinicians evaluate PID with a low threshold
claims.quote: health care providers should maintain a low threshold for the clinical diagnosis of PID

claims.text: non-albicans species, especially C. glabrata, appear to be increasing
claims.quote: Although Candida albicans is the main cause of VVC, the identification of non-Candida albicans Candida (NCAC) species, especially Candida glabrata, as the cause of this infection, appears to be increasing.

claims.text: VVC develops when the balance between Candida and host is disturbed
claims.quote: The development of VVC is usually attributed to the disturbance of the balance between Candida vaginal colonization and host environment by physiological or nonphysiological changes.

claims.text: hygiene, clothing and sexual habits proposed as behavioral risk factors; role unclear
claims.quote: Behavioral risk factors include use of oral contraceptives, intrauterine device, spermicides and condoms and some habits of hygiene, clothing and sexual practices. Despite a growing list of recognized risk factors, much remains to be elucidated

claims.quote: Worldwide, recurrent vulvovaginal candidiasis affects about 138 million women annually (range 103-172 million)

claims.quote: A time-location sample of 95 symptomatic women who purchased and presented with an over-the-counter antifungal product for immediate and personal treatment of presumed vulvovaginal candidiasis

claims.text: only 34 percent (about a third) actually had VVC; others BV, mixed vaginitis, normal, other
claims.quote: vulvovaginal candidiasis 33.7%, bacterial vaginosis 18.9%, mixed vaginitis 21.1%, normal 13.7%, other diagnoses 10.5%, and trichomonas vaginitis 2.1%.

claims.text: prior clinician diagnosis did not improve self-diagnosis accuracy
claims.quote: Women with a previous clinically based diagnosis of vulvovaginal candidiasis were not more accurate in diagnosing vulvovaginal candidiasis than women without a prior clinical diagnosis

claims.quote: Watery discharge and amine odor (negative "whiff" test) were good predictors of an alternative diagnosis, but, again, accuracy was poor.

claims.text: KOH and other quick microscopy only moderately accurate with false negatives and false positives

claims.text: triggers: antibiotics, diabetes, hormonal changes (pregnancy, high estrogen), immune dysfunction
claims.quote: Multiple factors contribute to both forms, including hormonal changes, diabetes, antibiotic use, immune dysfunction, and genetics.

claims.text: Candida lives harmlessly in the vagina of many healthy women
claims.quote: Asymptomatic vaginal colonization byis common, occurring in up to 20%–30% of healthy women

claims.text: switches between yeast and hyphal forms; filamentation helps tissue invasion
claims.quote: capable of transitioning between yeast, pseudo-hyphal, and hyphal forms, a process known as filamentation []. This morphological plasticity is tightly linked to its pathogenicity, as filamentation promotes tissue invasion

claims.text: significant symptoms and severe impact on quality of life
claims.quote: causing significant symptoms and severely impacting quality of life.

claims.text: non-albicans generally less sensitive to azoles
claims.quote: In general, most NAC species are less sensitive to azole drugs and more difficult to eradicate, in particular oral fluconazole.

claims.text: lactobacilli keep vagina acidic, protective against many germs; Candida tolerates acid
claims.quote: This acidic environment is protective against many potential pathogens, whereasspp. are acid-tolerant and can persist under these conditions

claims.text: microbiome disruption (antibiotics, hormonal changes) leads to overgrowth
claims.quote: microbiome disruptions, caused by factors like antibiotic use, hormonal fluctuations, or sexual activity, can lead to fungal overgrowth

claims.text: antibiotics a major contributor; disrupt protective vaginal bacteria (text, table, FAQ)
claims.quote: Antibiotic use is a major contributor to VVC by disrupting the protective vaginal microbiota

claims.text: higher estrogen from pregnancy, luteal phase, combined pill, menopause hormone therapy encourages colonization
claims.quote: Elevated estrogen levels, whether endogenous during pregnancy or luteal phase of the cycle, or exogenous from combined oral contraceptives or menopause hormone therapy, enhancespp. colonization

claims.text: combined pill linked to recurrent episodes; progestin-only pills and hormonal IUDs rarely; IUD itself can contribute
claims.quote: progestin-only contraceptive pill or hormonal (levonorgestrel-releasing) intrauterine contraceptive devices are rarely associated with increased risk, although the intrauterine contraceptive device itself can contribute to recurrent VVC

claims.text: combined pill associated with recurrent episodes
claims.quote: Hormonal fluctuations, particularly during the luteal phase, or in the form of combined contraceptive pill are also associated with RVVC episodes

claims.text: most cases in reproductive years; also adolescents and postmenopausal women
claims.quote: Although most cases occur in reproductive-aged women, VVC can also affect adolescents and postmenopausal women

claims.text: uncontrolled diabetes raises vaginal glucose, promoting overgrowth, and impairs immunity
claims.quote: In addition to causing immune dysfunction, uncontrolled diabetes elevates vaginal glucose levels promoting yeast overgrowth and proliferation

claims.text: SGLT2 inhibitors raise risk of recurrent infection
claims.quote: SLGT2 inhibitors used in the management of diabetes increase the risk for RVVC

claims.text: untreated HIV, corticosteroids, chemotherapy, other immunosuppressants raise risk
claims.quote: Conditions like untreated human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) and AIDS increase VVC risk due to T-cell dysfunction.

claims.text: immunosuppressive therapies raise risk
claims.quote: Various immunosuppressive therapies, including corticosteroids, chemotherapy, calcineurin and tumor necrosis factor-α inhibitors, antimetabolites, and monoclonal antibodies, compromise immune surveillance

claims.text: dry damaged vulvar skin from overwashing and feminine products a main modifiable risk factor
claims.quote: One of the main modifiable risk factors for VVC is dry and damaged vulval skin caused by overwashing and unnecessary use of feminine products

claims.text: douching discouraged though not an official risk factor
claims.quote: vaginal douching should be discouraged, although it is not an official risk factor for VVC

claims.text: tight synthetic clothing may trap heat and moisture
claims.quote: Tight synthetic clothing may trap heat and moisture, encouraging yeast growth.

claims.text: confirmatory tests important with poor response and recurrent infection
claims.quote: confirmatory tests are extremely helpful and essential in cases with poor or partial response and in RVVC

claims.text: vulvar dermatitis, lichen sclerosus, lichen simplex chronicus can mimic yeast
claims.quote: alternative diagnoses, such as vulval dermatitis, lichen sclerosus, or lichen simplex chronicus, which may mimic VVC symptoms

claims.text: boric acid not used in pregnancy
claims.quote: boric acid is contraindicated in pregnancy because of a lack of safety data

claims.text: prevention: minimize unnecessary antibiotic courses
claims.quote: A detailed history of antibacterial use should be obtained, with efforts to minimize unnecessary antibiotic courses

claims.text: prevention: control diabetes and other reversible causes
claims.quote: The initial step is to identify and address any reversible causes.

claims.text: prevention: avoid douching and feminine washes, wash without soap
claims.quote: Don’t use soaps, bubble baths, or shower gels. Avoid “feminine” washes and sprays.

claims.text: prevention: cotton underwear, avoid tight or synthetic clothing
claims.quote: Wear cotton underwear. Wash underwear with nonbiological products. Avoid wearing synthetic fabrics. Avoid wearing tight clothing.

claims.text: not an STI, rare partner transmission, partner treatment not recommended (FAQ)
claims.quote: VVC is not classified or considered a sexually transmitted infection, transmission between partners is rare, and partner treatment is not recommended

claims.text: luteal-phase flares and relief during menstruation (FAQ)
claims.quote: Clinically, women with RVVC often report symptom flares during the luteal phase and relief during menstruation.
